subject: Post-demo: handling of user prompts & derived outputs (what / where / TTL)
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Kerr <aisha.kerr@lawsonhealth.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@lawsonhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Oct 2029 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo — quick follow-up on prompt outputs, custody & TTL

Hi Aisha / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Per our demo and the security/discovery items you raised, I wanted to capture the concrete points we discussed about what Redwood stores from prompts and derived outputs, where those artifacts can live, and the control knobs available for TTL / export. I’m attaching a lightweight data-mapping template so you can indicate which fields you classify as PHI/PII.

Recap (high level):
- By default (hosted API):
  - Prompt text and model-generated outputs are kept in transient service logs and KV caches used for live inference and debugging. Default ephemeral TTL = 24 hours for content typed as non-legal/PII.
  - Customers can opt out of persistent logging for specific routes (no-write).
- For regulated workloads we discussed two options: Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) and Private (VPC/on-prem):
  - Dedicated: data remains in your dedicated tenant; audit logs retention is configurable at contract stage; can request 0-day persisted-token retention for prompt texts.
  - Private: you control storage endpoints (S3/MinIO) and KMS; Redwood control plane can be configured not to retain message contents.
- Key controls we highlighted: regional residency (we can pin inference & storage to eu-west-1), per-route TTL, redact-on-ingest pipelines, KMS/HSM options, and audit log exports (Syslog/Splunk/OCI).

Action items I promised:
1) Share data-mapping template (attached) — please mark any fields you want excluded from logs or classified as PHI.
2) Confirm desired residency (EU only?) and whether you need a contractual retention SLA (e.g., 0 hours / 7 days / 30 days).
3) We will provide SOC2 Type II redacted evidence and a short security brief tailored to Dedicated/Private options.

Next step proposal: If you can return the mapping by EOD Friday (10/11) we’ll have security draft + a scoped Mutual Action Plan ready for review by early next week. Marissa (cc) will pick up procurement cadence.

Attachments: data-mapping-template.xlsx (stub)

Thanks — talk soon,

— Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Aisha Kerr <aisha.kerr@lawsonhealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Oct 2029 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo — quick follow-up on prompt outputs, custody & TTL

Thanks, Mateo — helpful recap. A few clarifying questions before we fill the mapping: 

1) You mentioned a 24-hour default TTL for hosted — is that wall-clock TTL for persisted logs, or a retention window after which records are irreversibly deleted? We need to understand whether data can be exported internally during that window.
2) For outputs that include PHI (examples: patient name + free-text recommendation), can you confirm whether derived outputs are ever materialized to long-term storage in hosted mode (outside the 24h window) without an explicit contract?
3) If we route audit logs to our Splunk instance, can we choose a sampling rate or redact sensitive fields before export?

Also please confirm whether you can provide your most recent SOC2 Type II report and whether Redwood supports contract language for a 0-day persistence obligation for certain routes.

I'll loop Tom on the mapping; we aim to have an initial pass by Friday.

Best,
Aisha
Director, Trust & Privacy
Lawson Health
aisha.kerr@lawsonhealth.com

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Kerr <aisha.kerr@lawsonhealth.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@lawsonhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Oct 2029 16:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo — quick follow-up on prompt outputs, custody & TTL

Aisha — great questions, answered inline below. Quoting your points: 

> 1) You mentioned a 24-hour default TTL for hosted — is that wall-clock TTL for persisted logs, or a retention window after which records are irreversibly deleted? We need to understand whether data can be exported internally during that window.

- The default 24-hour TTL is a retention window for persisted logs we keep for debugging and metric aggregation. Within that window content is accessible to the service for support/debugging and can be exported if an internal support ticket requires it. We provide role-based access controls and audit trails for those actions. If you require that nothing be exportable, we recommend Dedicated or Private plus a contractual 0-day persistence for those routes.

> 2) For outputs that include PHI (examples: patient name + free-text recommendation), can you confirm whether derived outputs are ever materialized to long-term storage in hosted mode (outside the 24h window) without an explicit contract?

- No — in hosted mode we do not persist prompt+output pairs beyond the default retention period unless there is an explicit customer opt-in or a compliance/legal hold. Any customer who needs guaranteed non-persistence signs a standard addendum (we’ve included this in other SLAs).

> 3) If we route audit logs to our Splunk instance, can we choose a sampling rate or redact sensitive fields before export?

- Yes. We can configure log export to apply field-level redaction downstream and set sampling rates. For Splunk/Syslog exports we typically implement a lightweight transformation that strips fields flagged as PHI and replace them with deterministic tokens (if desired).

Attachments I’m adding: redwood-privacy-handbook.pdf (high-level controls) — delivering the SOC2 Type II redacted evidence via secure link in the next message.

If you’re comfortable we’ll: (a) provide SOC2 redacted report by EOD tomorrow, (b) draft a short contract addendum that includes a per-route retention SLA (0/7/30 days) and EU residency clause. Marissa will lead procurement.

— Mateo

Marissa / Aisha — quick confirmation from Security: we can contractually commit to 0-day persistence for named routes on Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted, we can add an isolation clause that prevents Redwood personnel from exporting payloads for specific customer routes (requires contract language + technical config), but true zero-exposure in hosted is only achievable via Dedicated or Private. SOC2 Type II redacted will be delivered via secure artifact link (we replace IPs/usernames before release) by tomorrow EOD.

Aisha — to help your internal risk team, I’ll include estimated delta in monthly cost if you pick Dedicated with a small reserved pool (ballpark: +$6k/month for the minimum config we discussed; final quote after MAP). Also — we can run a short EU-only pilot (14 days) in our eu-west region to validate residency and redaction pipelines before committing to Dedicated.

If that plan looks good we’ll schedule a 30-minute procurement call next week to review contract language and timelines.

— Karthik
